priority: HIGHEST — active, matched to all 7 test users, carries a live deadline, and the stored action is wrong
stored_url_verdict: WRONG ENTITY. That URL is the MAA MathFest programme's special-sessions page — MathFest is MAA's annual conference for mathematicians. It has nothing to do with the AMC student competitions. Correct URL: https://maa.org/student-programs/amc/
stored_deadline_verdict: REAL BUT MISLABELLED, AND IT IS NOT THE STUDENT'S DEADLINE. 2026-10-15 is the AMC 10/12 'Regular Registration Deadline: October 15, 2026 ($75 registration fee) - Final deadline for new competition managers'. It is a deadline for a SCHOOL to register as a competition site, not for a student to apply.
THE_CORE_PROBLEM: 'Students and parents do not register directly with the MAA.' The row is matched to 7 users and tells them a date they cannot act on. The real student action is: ask your school (or a local college, math circle or learning centre) to register as a competition manager — and to do it by the EARLY BIRD deadline, which is earlier and cheaper.
conflation_note: The stored title 'AMC - AIME' merges two different things. AMC 8/10/12 are open competitions a school hosts. AIME is INVITATIONAL — 'Students who perform exceptionally well on the AMC 10 and/or AMC 12 will be invited'. A student cannot enter AIME at all; they earn it. These should be separate records or at minimum the invitational nature must be explicit.

AMC_10_12.regular_note: Final deadline for NEW competition managers
AMC_10_12.bundle: $30 per bundle of ten student licenses; a student sitting both A and B needs two licenses

AMC_8.bundle: $25 per bundle of ten student licenses

earliest_actionable_note: 38 days from retrieval (2026-08-23) — and it is the school's action, not the student's. The stored 2026-10-15 is 15 days later and $20/registration dearer.

age_rules_verbatim.AMC_8: 'Middle school students in grades 8 and below, with a maximum age of under 15.5 years on the day of the competition.'
age_rules_verbatim.AMC_10: 'High school students in grades 10 and below, with a maximum age of under 17.5 years on the day of the competition.'
age_rules_verbatim.AMC_12: 'High school students in grades 12 and below, with a maximum age of under 19.5 years on the day of the competition.'

age_rules_note: Three different half-year age caps, each measured on competition day, plus a grade cap. The stored row has NO age or grade data at all. Note also 'Students may not take both AMC 10 and AMC 12 on the same day' and 'Students may only take the AMC 8 once each year'.
cost_note: DO NOT put a number in `cost`. The fees are institutional — $55/$75/$115 site registration paid by the competition manager, plus $30 (or $25) per ten student licences. What an individual student pays depends entirely on whether their school passes the cost on. This is the same institutional-vs-student distinction CEO drew for CMIMC's $5, and the same one that made IChO's $3,000 team fee wrong to store.

TURKIYE_ROUTE_RESOLVED.mechanism_verbatim: 'For the 2025-2026 competition cycle, the MAA AMC competitions will only be offered to schools with USA, Canada, APO/FPO/DPO mailing addresses, and schools registered with one of our AMC international partners.' 'International students participate in AMC competitions through one of our International Group Leaders (IGLs)... Students must register for the competitions through the IGL in the country they reside.'
TURKIYE_ROUTE_RESOLVED.turkiye_igl: Brad Hart — covering Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Croatia, Cyprus, Greece, Kosovo, Lithuania, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Turkey
TURKIYE_ROUTE_RESOLVED.caveat: The IGL list is headed 'International Group Leaders for 2025-26'. The 2026-27 list may differ — re-check before the cycle rather than assuming continuity.

eligibility_conflict_INHERITED_AND_STILL: oryn-ce flagged an unresolved conflict I did not resolve either: MAA describes USAMO/USAJMO eligibility in enrolment terms (studying in the USA/Canada) while other sources describe it as citizenship-based, and selection for the actual IMO team is a third and stricter rule again. I did not retrieve the full eligibility policy page this pass. This directly determines what a Turkish student can be told about progressing beyond AIME, so it needs resolving before any such advice is given.
fetch_method: Browser pane (maa.org returns 403 to WebFetch — oryn-ce reported the same, so the block is server-side, not specific to one tool)
recommendation: This row needs more than a URL fix. Minimum: correct official_url; relabel the deadline as an institutional registration deadline and add the 2026-09-30 early-bird date; add the three age/grade rules; record that students cannot self-register; add the AMC International route for non-US/Canada students. Ideally split AMC (open) from AIME (invitational).

priority: HIGH — active and matched to all 7 test users, but it is not an opportunity at all
finding: WRONG CORPUS — this is not a competition. It is an organisation that runs a DIRECTORY of other people's competitions.
evidence_verbatim: 'The Institute of Competition Sciences (ICS) was founded in 2012 to help transform learning into an exciting challenge for all students.' The homepage presents 'Featured Competitions' linking out to third-party programmes (MATE ROV Competition, NASA ORBIT, Virtual Supreme Court).
what_a_student_would_experience: A student told to 'apply' lands on a listings site. There is a student sign-up, but it registers you for the ICS platform, not for any competition — the competitions themselves belong to other organisers and are entered elsewhere.
the_irony_worth_naming: ICS is precisely the class of source my own brief treats as DISCOVERY ONLY — an aggregator whose listings are leads to be verified, never facts to publish. Having the aggregator itself stored as an opportunity inverts that: it turns the index into an entry in the index. It also explains a pattern I met repeatedly tonight — competitionsciences.org kept surfacing in search results for real competitions (BL4S, SJWP, Slingshot), because it is a directory of them.
proposed_action: Remove from the opportunities corpus (status='disabled' or delete). It is a legitimate and possibly useful website; it is not something a student applies to. If anything it belongs in a discovery-source list for the research pipeline, not in the student-facing catalogue.

stored_url_verdict: NOT A PROGRAMME PAGE. It is a direct link to an asset-server PDF — a SPANISH-language '7 Tips' handout, and the filename itself says 'Draft-2'. A student clicking through gets a draft tips sheet in a language they may not read, with no way to enter anything.
organization: National Geographic Society (supported by Allen Family Philanthropies)
age_note: Reaches down to 13 — one of the few genuinely open international opportunities for the youngest end of ORYN's band.
what_to_submit_verbatim: 'one-minute videos describing their ideas for solving environmental issues'
format_note: A one-minute video is an unusually low-effort entry format for a real award. For a student with little profile history and little time, the effort-to-value ratio here is among the best found in this lane.
eligible_countries: NOT ESTABLISHED. The official page says 'Slingshot has expanded globally' but never states an eligibility rule by country. Per the placement test, an expansion claim in narrative prose is NOT an eligibility statement. Recorded as unknown.
deadline_note: The 2026 cycle closed (secondary sources give 6 February 2026 — 198 days past at retrieval; NOT officially confirmed and not stored). The official page references '2026 Award Recipients' and 'the next Slingshot Challenge' with no date. Do not infer a next deadline.
awards: NOT STATED on the official page. Secondary sources describe five $10,000 Top Honors and ten $1,000 Significant Achievement awards — NOT officially confirmed, recorded here only as an unverified claim.

recommendation: Fix official_url and title. Genuinely worth keeping — it is age-13-accessible, low-effort and well-funded — but its country eligibility and award amounts are unverified, so it should not be presented as confirmed worldwide.

priority: HIGH — active, matched to all 7 users, and it is a league rather than an event
finding: NOT A SINGLE COMPETITION. MLH is an organisation that sanctions and supports many independent hackathons — the same category error as the ICS row (CR1-121), though less severe because MLH is at least in the hackathon business rather than being a pure directory.
evidence_verbatim: 'We help run the global hacker community'; the site advertises '1000+ Annual Events' across '100 Countries' and lists 'Upcoming Hackathons'.
consequence: There is no single thing to apply to and no single deadline. A student told to 'apply to Major League Hacking' has been given an unactionable instruction; the real action is 'find an MLH-sanctioned hackathon near you or online, and register for that one'.
eligibility: NOT STATED — the site does not say whether participants must be university students, high school students, or both, and states no age restriction. This matters: hackathon leagues frequently restrict to 18+ or to university enrolment for insurance reasons, and MLH's own high-school-facing programming is not described on the page retrieved.
deadline_note: No single deadline exists by construction — 'many separate events' each with their own registration.
note_on_url: The stored URL points at a 2026 season events listing, which at least is the right kind of page — unlike the ICS and Slingshot rows, this one is not pointing somewhere wrong, it is pointing at a LIST.
proposed_action: Either (a) recategorise as a discovery source rather than an opportunity, or (b) keep but relabel so the student action is 'browse MLH-sanctioned events' rather than 'apply'. Also resolve whether high schoolers are eligible at all before it is recommended to a 14-18 audience — that is currently unknown and is the single most decision-relevant unknown on this row.
unresolved: Whether high school students may participate in MLH events at all.

priority: MEDIUM — active and matched to all 7 users; genuine competition, but its own page says the shown details are stale
organization: iGEM Foundation, Inc. — a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit, Cambridge MA USA and Paris, France
dedupe_note: NOT a duplicate of row 931e7fc2 ('International Genetically Engineered Machine Competition (iGEM)', competition.igem.org/). CEO verified this independently: 931e7fc2 is the umbrella/collegiate product and is already under_review with 0 matches; this row is the high-school product and is correctly live. Two audiences, one organisation, distinguished by URL path — the same shape as the Bocconi case another lane found. The system handled this one correctly, and merging them would have buried the high-school product inside the university one.
cycle_status_verbatim: 'COMING SOON... Preparations for the 2026 iGEM Competition are underway. This page will be updated soon. Below are details from the 2025 Competition season for reference.'
cycle_status_note: UNUSUALLY HONEST SOURCE — the operator explicitly labels its own visible content as prior-season reference material. That is exactly the disclosure most stale pages omit (compare Özyeğin's stale 'APPLICATIONS ARE NOW OPENED' banner). Everything below is therefore 2025-season fact, not current fact, and must not be stored as current.

2025_season_reference.jamboree: 'All teams are encouraged to attend the event from October 28-31, 2025, at the Paris Convention Centre, Paris, France.'
2025_season_reference.white_list_rule: 'Starting in 2025, high school teams must ensure that their projects use only the organisms and components specified in the current iGEM White List.'
2025_season_reference.villages: High school teams choose a Village and display alongside collegiate teams at the Grand Jamboree.
2025_season_reference.support: Registered teams receive a Parts Distribution Kit; a Mentorship Program exists for new teams; a High School PI Network supports supervising adults.

team_structure_note: Team-based and adult-supervised — iGEM refers throughout to teams with PIs (Principal Investigators). A lone student cannot enter; this needs a school or institution behind it. Not explicitly stated as a rule on this page, but it is the structure the whole page describes.
cost_note: NO FEE STATED on this page. iGEM is known to charge substantial team registration fees, so a NULL here is a genuine risk of reading as free — but I found no figure on the official high-school page and will not publish an unsourced one. HIGH PRIORITY to resolve: this is a team competition with international travel to a Jamboree, so the true cost to a school is likely significant.
eligible_countries: NOT STATED. iGEM is plainly international (HQ in both the US and France, teams worldwide) but no eligibility rule by country appears on this page.
fetch_method: Browser pane (WebFetch returned an empty body — the page is JS-rendered)
recommendation: Keep. Genuine, prestigious, research-producing synthetic-biology competition. But record it as date_not_announced with 2025 details marked as reference, and prioritise finding the team fee — an unknown cost on a team competition requiring travel to Paris is the exact gap this lane has been documenting all night.

priority: HIGHEST — active, matched to all 7 users, stores NO deadline, and registration actually closes in ~4 weeks
organization: HMMT — 'entirely student-organized, by students at Harvard, MIT, and nearby schools, many of whom are HMMT alumni themselves'
THE_URGENT_FACT: The site's own news banner reads: 'Registration is open! Applications close on September 20. Apply here.' Today is 2026-08-23, so that is roughly 28 days away — and the live row carries no deadline at all while being matched to every test user.
deadline_year_caveat: The banner says 'September 20' WITHOUT a year. I am reading it as 2026 because registration is open now (August 2026) and the next tournament is 7 November 2026. That inference is strong but it IS an inference — the year is not printed. Confirm before this date is written to production.
registration_structure: ORGANISATION-BASED. The registration flow is: 'Step 1: Register your organization' → 'Step 2: Select an organization' → 'Step 3: Choose a tournament' → 'Step 4: Create/update an application' → 'Step 5: Invite your students to your organization'. A student cannot enter alone; a school, club or team must register and then invite them.
cost_evidence: A fee is not quoted on the pages retrieved, but the registration flow includes 'Step 6: Apply for financial aid' — which establishes that participation costs money and that need-based support exists. Recording cost as NULL with this note rather than as free.
scale_and_prestige_verbatim: 'Founded in 1998, HMMT is one of the largest and most prestigious high school competitions in the world. Each tournament draws close to 1000 students from around the globe, including top scorers at national and international olympiads.'
eligible_countries: NOT STATED as a rule, but 'students from around the globe' is asserted in the About text. Note per the placement test this sits in descriptive prose, not in an eligibility statement — so international participation is evidently real in practice but is NOT a published eligibility rule. Recorded as such.
team_scoring_note: 'A full team is considered as 6 students for November's tournament and 8 students for February's tournament... it is advantageous to have a full team.' Relevant to a student from a small school — an incomplete team is allowed but scored at a disadvantage.
FRAUD_WARNING_WORTH_SURFACING: HMMT publishes an unusual notice directly relevant to ORYN's international users: 'HMMT does not partner with any organizations connected to competing teams. Any non-HMMT person or group claiming to represent HMMT is untruthful, especially if they claim to represent HMMT in a specific country. Please report all such organizations to us at request@hmmt.org.' In other words, entities have been falsely presenting themselves as HMMT's national representative. A Turkish or other international student is exactly who such an intermediary would target, and this is precisely the kind of protective fact a career advisor should carry. It also cuts against the national-route pattern found everywhere else tonight: for HMMT there is NO legitimate country representative, and anyone claiming to be one is a red flag.
awards: Prizes to the ten highest-scoring individuals overall, top ten on each individual test, five highest-scoring teams on Team Round, five on Guts Round; top ten teams overall named Sweepstakes winners. 'Ties will not be broken.'
recommendation: Highest-priority enrichment in this batch alongside AMC. Add the 2026-09-20 registration deadline (after confirming the year), both tournament dates, the organisation-based registration structure, and the fraud notice. A row matched to every user with a four-week-out deadline and no deadline stored is the worst combination in the corpus.

priority: HIGH — active and matched to all 7 users while being the wrong entity entirely
finding: WRONG ENTITY — this is a professional career-achievement award, not a student opportunity. It is nominated, not entered, and its nominees are established researchers and institutions.
corroboration: oryn-ce researched this independently before their lane closed and reached the same conclusion via kva.se (the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences) and stockholmwaterfoundation.org, recording it as D with the note 'this is not a student/youth award'. Two lanes, separate evidence, same verdict.
the_real_youth_award: The genuine student equivalent is the **Stockholm Junior Water Prize**, which I researched separately as CR1-036: ages 15-20, federated across 39 countries including Türkiye (national organiser: Devlet Su İşleri, Ankara), research-based, and it accepts social-science and policy projects. That is a NEW record for a DIFFERENT entity — not a correction of this row. Both facts need to land together, or the corpus loses a real opportunity while keeping a fake one.
why_it_matters_now: This row is status='active' and appears in opportunity_matches for all 7 test users. So ORYN is currently capable of suggesting that a 16-year-old pursue a lifetime-achievement award for water researchers — while the actual youth prize they could enter is absent from the corpus. That inversion is the clearest single illustration of the identity-verification failure mode: the names differ by one word.
proposed_action: Remove from the student-facing corpus (status='disabled'), and add CR1-036 (Stockholm Junior Water Prize) in its place.
scope_note: This row was oryn-ce's while their lane was open; CEO transferred competition ownership to me when it closed. I am recording the removal proposal rather than leaving it orphaned, and crediting their prior work.

organization: Lewis Center for the Arts, Princeton University
eligibility_verbatim: 'Eligibility for this annual playwriting contest is limited to U.S. or international students in the eleventh grade.'
THE_KEY_RULE: ELEVENTH GRADE ONLY. Not 9-12, not 'high school' — a single year group. A 10th or 12th grader is ineligible. The live row stores no grade data at all while being matched to all 7 test users, so it is being offered to students who cannot enter.
eligibility_placement: 'U.S. or international students' appears INSIDE the eligibility sentence itself — the strongest possible placement, and an unusually explicit inclusion of international students for a US university contest. Meets the placement test cleanly.
international_note: Worth contrasting with the US research tier (CR1-094), where nearly everything excludes non-US students. This is a US university contest that says the opposite in plain words.
judging_verbatim: 'Each year a guest playwright serves as contest judge.'
deadline_note: No date published; the page states only that submissions are currently closed. Contest is described as annual.
category_note: This is an ARTS contest, not academic research. Legitimately a competition, but it should surface for a student with writing/theatre interests — never as a research or STEM recommendation.
clean_negative_result: The same official page announces that the 'Leonard L. Milberg '53 High School Poetry Prize' was DISCONTINUED after the 2024-25 academic year. I checked the corpus for it (by title, by 'poetry', and by arts.princeton.edu domain) and it is NOT present — so there is no stale discontinued row to clean up. Recording the negative because 'I checked and there was nothing' is a different and more useful statement than silence.
recommendation: Add eligible_grades=['11'] and set cycle_status='closed'. The grade rule is the whole point of this row — without it ORYN recommends a contest to students who are structurally barred.

subject: I called the 9 unverified rows 'the actual harm surface'. That was too broad — and the correction inverts my priority order.
what_i_claimed: That the 9 `unverified` + `active` competition rows matched to all 7 test users were 'the rows actually reaching students', and I titled the handoff section 'THE ACTUAL HARM SURFACE'.
what_is_actually_true: They do NOT reach core recommendations. `verification_state='unverified'` is filtered out on the recommendation path. They are visible in Browse only, because `status='active'`.
verified_from_the_code_not_taken_on_trus: CEO reported this; I checked it in the product rather than accepting it, and the code confirms them at TWO layers: (1) `lib/counselor/state.ts:143` restricts the eligible-matches query with `.eq("verification_state", "verified_current")`; (2) `lib/counselor/eligibility.ts:45` re-checks the same condition as defence-in-depth, returning `known_ineligible` with 'This opportunity is not currently verified.' The comment there cites spec §37's 'unverified opportunities never appear as verified' invariant.
why_i_got_it_wrong: I read the presence of `opportunity_matches` rows as 'these reach students'. A match row is not a recommendation — the counselor filters at read time, and the match table is upstream of that filter. Same class of mistake as the `status` one earlier tonight: I inferred reach from the table I happened to query instead of from the gating function. My own working memory says to derive metrics from the product code before quoting them, and I did not do it that time.
THE_CONSEQUENCE_IS_A_PRIORITY_INVERSION: The batch that actually reaches students is the OTHER one — the 8 `verified_current` rows with zero eligibility data (CR1-130…137): Breakthrough Junior Challenge, USACO, The Earth Prize, The Concord Review, Blue Ocean, DECA, HOSA, Purple Comet. Those pass the verification gate and feed recommendations. The 9 unverified rows are Browse-only and should be fixed second, not first.
what_still_stands: Every individual finding in the unverified batch is unchanged and still worth fixing: Stockholm Water Prize is still the wrong entity while the real youth prize is absent; ICS is still a directory rather than an opportunity; Nat Geo Slingshot's URL is still a Spanish draft PDF; AMC's deadline is still the school's rather than the student's; HMMT's ~2026-09-20 registration close is still unstored. What changes is urgency, not validity — a student browsing the catalogue can still hit all of them.
sharpest_single_item_after_reordering: Breakthrough Junior Challenge (CR1-130). CEO measured it as `highly_selective`, cost 0, deadline already stored, and it DOES reach core recommendations — so the missing piece is not the date but the eligibility, above all that the video, script and voiceover must be in English. For a Turkish student that is a real capability gate and it has to be said before they spend the effort, not after. 23 days out.
